purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the fourth Ruleset Card — the variety-engine proof (4 of ~34 types). Slice shape mirrors the three shipped g1 siblings: one query tide with a world-map baseline that has no local hour, an amplification volley as the surprise-with-composition beat, and a finale built on the level's authored cruelty ('Nothing is down. Everything is unreachable.'). Deliberately RULES-FREE (no rules block): §2.24 rule-carrier values stay in the g1 slices until the batch-D rule-adapter pass reads them for cross-type tables.
determinismNote: Authored + seeded (§7.13): same seed replays identical arrival order; the sim core owns jitter streams off this seed.
rolesNote: Every entry carries `role` = its PRIMARY threat role from threats/registry-core.json `roles[0]` (§2.1 Threat Role Taxonomy, 12-role vocabulary); wave `denominations` arrays are entry-derived, and every hard wave draws exactly TWO fronts (§2.1 Two-Front Law / §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). Cold Start Minute governs the first 90s of sim-time: handover no threat, one FREE conversion, signature constraint asserts harmlessly with telegraph (§1.9). On this line the harmless assertion is a probe drizzle reading itself as zone-transfer curiosity, not volume — the grey blur barely notices.

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the card's signature volley, early and unmissable. Two-Front (§2.24): the amplification barrage spends bandwidth (query PPS against PoP capacity) AND reputation (the abuse desk lights up because your resolvers are the reflectors); the open-resolver conscription feeds it (§2.12 'Reflection Conscription' — a node blasting a cone off-map while an angry abuse-complaint glyph flies in).
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the RRL tuning, the negative-cache policy, the first extra PoP all get their window here. The drop is not clean air — free-tier tenants running table-scan queries against their own giant zones spend cash-per-query COGS (§2.12 'Free-Tier COGS Leak': 'the signature non-attack problem: the product is nearly free and it costs you not'), while the probe drizzle continues mapping your transfer posture.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, DNS variant: the rollover-day lands — a fleet-wide scheduled event that splits traffic toward whatever the player forgot to rotate (Splitter debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat; unseen in waves 1-3) — and the zone-change ticket avalanche (Swarm, hands) arrives inside the same incident window, so the second-incident multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24). Two fronts: data-integrity (a signing or zone mistake is correctness debt, the card's '— and correctness' scarce tail) x hands (every customer's TTL bet wants a human).
waves.secondIncident: ticket avalanche arrives inside the rollover-day incident window -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the card's cruelty, mechanised: nothing new arrives at full volume — the abandonment spiral (Healer/Spawner, second fresh role of the slice's cadence) compounds the wave-4 smudge while validating resolvers quietly give up on you, the water-torture sipper grinds the cache (§2.12 random-subdomain flood: 'the cache is beaten, every query comes to you'), and the rollover day's split traffic continues. Hard wave draws TWO fronts — concurrency x reputation — per §2.24. The signature moment fires inside this wave if the key calendar went unread all quarter: 'Nothing is down. Everything is unreachable. Your monitoring, which uses a non-validating resolver, says green.' (§1.3). The world-map stake is the Dyn-2016 beat: you are attacked because of WHO your customers are, and hundreds of companies go down publicly with your name attached (§1.3). Win check: free-to-paid conversion held >=1.5% across the window while the free tier stayed survivable.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
